## a1105be40960

**Possible shortcut, reproduced on generated data and separated by a real-rule counterexample.** Generator SHA-256 `a28d9ce3d0524cdce7ff44eb7c21a82e4e8a0c9aa6435d0a4a81316f61f3979b` replaces the canonical concentric hollow frames with scattered solid rectangles. In 200 samples per band (600 total), every input was distinct and validator-clean, every color-4 component was a solid rectangle, and bbox-area ordering was therefore identical to pixel-count ordering in 600/600 cases. A learner can use “select the k-th largest object by number of colored cells” instead of the selected rule's bbox-area measure. See `checks/audit/a1105be40960/shortcut_census.json`.

I constructed a validator-accepted distinction in `checks/audit/a1105be40960/input.json`: object A is a hollow 5×5 frame with bbox area 25 and 16 cells; object B is a solid 4×5 rectangle with bbox area 20 and 20 cells; one blue cell sets `k=1`. The supported Racket apply command executed rule hash `b3ce44730a7b` and recolored object A (`racket.json`). The pixel-count rival recolors object B (`pixel_count_rival.json`). Thus the shortcut is genuinely different from selected authority, not merely a verbal concern.

Domain qualification: the counterexample passes the current validator and uses the canonical task's hollow-frame topology, but it lies outside the selected generator summary's all-solid distribution. This is therefore a data/validator-domain gap and possible training shortcut, not a claim that an emitted sample is mislabeled. No fix was made.

## a1105be40960

**Reproduced semantic shortcut — bbox area aliases pixel count.** Generator SHA-256 `a28d9ce3d0524cdce7ff44eb7c21a82e4e8a0c9aa6435d0a4a81316f61f3979b`; executed rule hash `b3ce44730a7b`. The intended rule selects the `k`-th largest yellow component by bounding-box area, but every yellow object in 60/60 sampled default draws across easy, medium, and hard was a solid rectangle. Thus bbox area equals cell count and a pixel-count learner receives no distinguishing evidence. The same rival matches all five canonical labelled pairs.

A retained validator-accepted counterexample separates the hypotheses: one sparse L has bbox area 16 and 7 cells, while one solid 3×3 has bbox area 9 and 9 cells, with one blue selector (`k=1`). The Racket authority recolors the sparse L; the pixel-count rival recolors the 3×3. `self_check` returns no errors. Evidence: `checks/audit/a1105be40960/input.json`, `validator.json`, `racket.json`, and `shortcut_probe.json`.

This is a training-data defect, not a label defect. A repair should generate non-solid objects with deliberately crossed bbox-area/cell-count rankings and declare the pixel-count rival in the semantic contract. I did not edit the audit target.

triage.reason: 135219aecdb4 invalid-type coercion advisory at API boundary; produced inputs/labels not shown defective, preserve matching reviewed_safe source. a1105be40960 bbox-area/cell-count contrast validator-lawful but outside sampled solid-object support; matching source already unsafe, retain coverage follow-up.

## a1105be40960

**Classification: Reproduced teaching shortcut.** Generator SHA-256 `a28d9ce3d0524cdce7ff44eb7c21a82e4e8a0c9aa6435d0a4a81316f61f3979b`; no declared `RULE_HASH` in the reviewed generator (executed/catalog authority hash `b3ce44730a7b`).

All 300 sampled generated lessons—100 per difficulty—used solid rectangles. Consequently each object's bounding-box area equals its cell count, and a mass-ranking rival is observationally identical to the intended bounding-box-area ranking on every sampled input. Evidence: `checks/audit/a1105be40960/domain_probe.json`.

The validator-accepted 11×11 witness `checks/audit/a1105be40960/input.json` contains an object with bounding-box area 9 and mass 5 and another with bounding-box area 6 and mass 6, with selector `k=1`. The authority selects the first by bounding-box area (`racket.json`), while the rival selects the second by cell count (`rival_cell_count.json`). `metadata.json` confirms `self_check` accepted the input and records the reproduction command. This is a concrete lesson-distribution defect: generated demonstrations do not teach the ranking quantity the authority actually uses.
